correctness.rationale: For a finite local nonfield, Z(R)=m and the published total-graph theorem decomposes the graph by m-cosets. After deleting zero, T0 is K_{s-1} plus either q-1 copies of K_s or (q-1)/2 copies of K_{s,s}. Zero forcing is additive over components; direct forcing arguments give Z(K_t)=t-1 for t>=2, Z(K_{s,s})=2s-2, and Z(K_1)=1. Block matrices J on cliques and [[0,J],[J,0]] on bicliques give rank q for s>=3, while the s=2 graph K1 union K2 has a rank-one witness. The universal inequality M<=Z closes equality. Exact enumeration and rational-rank replay on representative local rings corroborate the formulas.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact algebra-to-inverse-eigenvalue dictionary for a natural graph introduced specifically to remove the distinguished zero vertex. For s>=3 the real minimum rank is exactly the residue-field order, graph order then recovers maximal-ideal size, zero forcing attains maximum nullity, and every minimum forcing set has a precise coset-transversal description. The s=2 boundary is exact and changes the minimum rank by one.
